sections.name: File setup, ROOTS
sections.title: Scan setup and file types
sections.what: Imports file reading tools and the money-term checker, lists the folders to scan and the file extensions that count as text.
sections.why: Limits the scan to the parts of the project that could show or store money-related content.
sections.watch_out: A new top-level folder or file type is skipped silently unless it is added here.

sections.name: walk
sections.title: Finding text files
sections.what: Walks through each scanned folder, including subfolders, and collects every file whose name ends with a listed text type.
sections.why: Makes sure the audit covers all relevant files without listing them by hand.
sections.watch_out: Files with an unlisted extension are not checked at all.

sections.name: no-money audit
sections.title: No-money audit
sections.what: Scans the collected files for payment, UPI, QR code, wallet, entry-fee, prize and similar terms, skipping deny-list files. Confirms that only the verifier's deny-list is exempt, that the database schema has no fee, prize, wallet, payment, balance, payout, deposit or amount fields, and that the checker flags money wording while allowing disclaimers such as no entry fees.
sections.why: Likely reason: the product's rules rule out money features, so the check guards that rule over time.
sections.watch_out: The schema pattern matches only certain column names and types, so a money field with another name could pass.

summary: Scans the app's source, data schema, configuration and public files to make sure no payment, prize, wallet or entry-fee language or fields have been added.
purpose: Enforces that the product has no money features, as a standing check.
why: Likely reason: the project is meant to be free of money features, and this check catches accidental additions.
how: Lists the folders to scan and the file types to include. Collects every matching file, reads it, skips files that declare themselves as deny-lists, and checks each remaining file for money terms. It also checks the only exempt file, checks the database schema for money-like column names, and checks that the term checker itself works.
inputs: Files in the src, public, prisma, config and scripts folders and the schema file.
outputs: Pass or fail. On failure, the list of files and terms that were found.
risks: A new folder or file type is not scanned unless added to the list. A money word spelled differently may pass. Column names matching the schema pattern can slip through if named differently.
debug: Read the failure message, which names the file and the term. If a new folder is in use, add it to the scanned list. If the term is in a legitimate disclaimer, the checker is the place to adjust.
